title: Additional Travel Rules — Travel on Sponsored Projects: From Approval to Reimbursement
display_label: Additional Travel Rules — Travel on Sponsored Projects: From Approval to Reimbursement
content:
Additional Travel Rules

From the ORA eTraining module "Travel on Sponsored Projects: From Approval to Reimbursement" (lesson 4 of 8).
Supplemental Travel Policies
Hotel & Other Lodging
Travel destination must be more than 40 miles from MSU campus for lodging expenses to be allowable. AirBNB is prohibited. Tax charges & lodging fees are allowed for hotel/lodging expenses. If the traveler does not have a University Purchasing Card at check-in, an admin with a p-card tied to your grant must submit a Credit Card Authorization Form prior to your stay. Check with your chosen hotel for further details. Hotel housekeeping tips will be reimbursed up to $1 per day. Travelers are responsible for all incidental charges, including room service and streaming options. Incidental charges are not allowed to be charged to either a grant or state-fund.
Car Rental
Do not purchase additional insurance (MSU has basic coverage). Rental contracts should be signed "Traveler Name, Morgan State University, State of Maryland" to be covered by MSU. It is encouraged to use Globetrotter for car rental, but not mandatory.
Uber/Taxi
Keep original receipts for any taxi fare. Tips should be limited to no more than 20% of the total fare cost. These costs should be listed under "ground transportation" on the TL form.
International Travel
International travel is commonly not allowable on grants unless permission is granted by the sponsor via the Notice of Award (NOA) or written notification. When submitting international travel request forms, be sure to include a copy of your project's NOA as supporting documentation.
Complete the content above before moving on.
Knowledge Check
Knowledge check: A psychology professor plans to attend the 2025 American Psychological Association (APA) Conference with their Co-Principal Investigator. While the conference hotel charges $250 per night for a single room, the professor identified an Airbnb that can accommodate both attendees for $300 per night. Is the professor permitted to choose the more cost-effective Airbnb option?
  - Yes  [incorrect]
  - No  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: While it may appear more cost-effective, university policy does not allow Airbnb accommodations due to liability and risk management concerns.
